title: White House Bars Reporters from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico in Escalating Press Freedom Battle
snippet: In a dramatic escalation of tensions between the White House and the press corps, journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico were denied entry and had their credentials revoked Saturday following a ban declared by President Donald Trump.
content:
WASHINGTON — In a swift crackdown on White House press access, reporters from three major news organizations were turned away at the gates on Saturday morning after President Donald Trump revoked their credentials, escalating a high-stakes battle over First Amendment protections.

Correspondents from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico were informed that their security badges had been disabled as they attempted to cover the administration. The move follows a Friday announcement by President Trump declaring an immediate ban on the outlets over what he characterized as persistent "fake news" coverage.

Credentials Confiscated at the Gate

MS NOW White House reporter Akayla Gardner and CNN senior White House reporter Betsy Klein both went on air Saturday to report that their hard passes were no longer valid. Gardner recounted passing through initial security checkpoints before an officer informed her that her badge had been disabled and needed to be confiscated, noting the command "was above him."

Politico confirmed that its White House reporter, Cheyenne Haslett, was similarly turned away and had her badge taken by security officers.

Media Outlets Vow First Amendment Defense

The revocation sparked immediate, forceful backlash from news executives, who framed the administration's actions as an authoritarian challenge to constitutional press freedoms.

"We stand by her and all reporters here covering the White House," Politico Editor-in-Chief Jonathan Greenberger said in a statement to his newsroom. "We will vigorously defend our First Amendment rights."

CNN released a statement reiterating its commitment to public-interest reporting: "We will not be deflected from our duty to hold the government and other public bodies to account." CNN media analyst Brian Stelter called the move "a direct threat to press freedom in the United States" and a critical test for free speech rights nationwide.

MS NOW also vowed legal action if necessary, stating: "The White House belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars. MS NOW intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy."

Pattern of Punitive Action

The ban is the latest in a series of administrative, regulatory, and legal maneuvers targeting news organizations critical of the administration. On Friday, Trump defended his directive during an Oval Office briefing, dismissing the three outlets and suggesting additional media organizations could face similar restrictions.

The incident follows a similar confrontation last year when the administration barred Associated Press journalists from the Oval Office and Air Force One after the wire service declined to adopt the administration's directive to refer to the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America." The AP subsequently filed a federal lawsuit over the access restriction, a case that remains active in the courts.
